reason: Matthew Mejia (E034) requests write access to Payroll. Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict: Most notes say full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

The Security note says they looked up employment type and security training in their own database. Note 1 (HR?) says they looked up employment type too. Hmm.

Note 1: role looked up, employment type looked up in own database → says full_time.
Note 6: role NOT looked up in own database (same value as others), employment type looked up → contractor with basic security training.

Who is the source of truth for employment type? Typically HR owns employment records. Note 1 says employment type looked up in own database before writing - that's probably HR. Note 6 is Security - Security looked up employment type in their own database.

Hmm, this is the classic conflicting facts scenario. We need to decide which to trust. The policy says contractors can have read or write with advanced training; never admin. Full-time up to write.

If he's full-time Analyst: requested write ≤ write max → grant write.
If he's contractor with basic training: max is read, request write > max → grant read.

Which fact do we trust? The task is to make the decision based on the info. There's a disagreement. Typically, HR is the authoritative source for employment type. Note 1 (HR presumably) looked it up in own database and says full_time. Security looked up and says contractor.
